subject.title: Gemini models output inline buttons as raw JSON text instead of using tool format

question: Should OpenClaw support raw `[[...]]` inline-button JSON in model final text as a constrained Gemini fallback, or require Gemini/provider prompting to use the existing typed message-tool presentation path?
rationale: Current source confirms the delivery gap for raw final text, but parsing model-authored JSON into controls would add a new fallback syntax across channel delivery and transcript state rather than only repairing the existing typed contract.

options.title: Accept Narrow Raw Fallback
options.body: Allow a constrained parser only if the linked PR or replacement is transcript-safe, rebased, and proven with redacted live Gemini/Telegram evidence.

options.title: Require Typed Presentation
options.body: Reject raw final-text parsing and fix provider or prompt routing so Gemini emits `message(action=send)` with structured buttons.

options.title: Defer Until Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause implementation until a reporter or maintainer supplies a reproducible Gemini/Telegram trace.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Raw Fallback
recommendation.body: Allow a constrained parser only if the linked PR or replacement is transcript-safe, rebased, and proven with redacted live Gemini/Telegram evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the typed presentation contract and Telegram button rendering history where `steipete` has the strongest path ownership signal.
